payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit established the corrected cycle life at 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee. The prototype’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh-scale manufacturing, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
